rooms.name: Road (west)
notes: You are on the road, looking east: white render, a timber-batten car gate and a batten gate for people.
The pedestrian gate and the main door both sit in the 3rd–4th of the nine west-side padas, counted from the south-west (Sugriva and Pushpadanta), the ones Vastu recommends for a west-facing entrance.

rooms.name: Front garden & gates
notes: The 0.9 m front setback stays unpaved: a planted bed with a frangipani and stepping stones from the gate.

rooms.name: Laundry nook
notes: The laundry sits under the upper flight, inside the locked foyer: a front-load washer and a utility sink at the end of the nook, a basket and shelves on the spine wall.
There is 2.2–2.9 m of headroom where you stand, and 1.6–1.8 m over the machine. A cupboard under the half landing holds the ironing board and cleaning things.
Clothes still dry on the roof deck. Under-stair use at stilt level should be confirmed with the authority, as stilts are meant for parking.

rooms.name: Stair
notes: One U-turn (dog-leg) stair, stacked in the same spot on every floor at the front south-west corner. You arrive at the front and the next flight starts from the same landing, so you never walk through a floor to go up.

Each storey has 17 risers of about 185 mm (an odd number, as Vastu prefers) and 250 mm treads: 9 risers east along the north lane, a 1.0 m half landing where you turn, then 8 risers back west along the south wall.
It climbs east, turns south and comes back west: clockwise in plan, in the south-west, the arrangement Vastu prefers for stairs.

Flights are 1.0 m wide. The room side is an open screen of slim black-steel balusters (gaps under 100 mm) from the floor up to a timber handrail, so light passes through. There are handrails on both sides of every flight, and a glass skylight over the stairwell on the roof.

Structure: a 115 mm RCC spine wall runs up the middle and an RCC wall closes the east side. Each flight is a waist slab from the floor beam to the half-landing beam. The core also stiffens the frame against sway.

rooms.name: Entrance foyer
notes: The main door is 1.06 × 2.40 m, rectangular, with the same vertical timber battens as the car gate. It faces west and now sits right at the front, 2.4 m from the gate.

Step in and the stair starts straight ahead: turn left onto the first flight. The door locks the stair and the whole house above. A glass screen lets the car porch light in without opening the stair to it.
A shoe cabinet and bench stand beside the door, and the laundry nook opens off the foyer.

rooms.name: Entry porch
notes: A short planted porch under the first-floor loggia, with a black-and-white checkerboard floor, leads from the gate to the main door.

rooms.name: Car porch (stilt)
notes: Your car parks in the north-west, which Vastu prefers for vehicles. Moving the stair to the front frees the whole back half of the stilt.
The underground sump sits under the north-east end, where Vastu wants water storage below ground.

rooms.name: Bike bay & workshop
notes: The space behind the stair is now a covered bay for the motorcycle, bicycles and a workbench, opening straight off the car porch.

rooms.name: Store
notes: A store opening off the car porch for tools, pump controls and garden things.

rooms.name: North side setback
notes: Kept open and unpaved. Vastu favours more openness to the north and east, and this strip lets the north windows breathe.

rooms.name: Rear setback
notes: A 0.7 m rear setback for the rainwater recharge pit and the kitchen chimney outlet.

rooms.name: First-floor loggia
notes: A 1.35 m deep loggia behind two arches, reached from the hall by a 1.2 m steel-framed slider. It shades the west glass.

rooms.name: Common bathroom
notes: A full bathroom in the north-west: WC, basin and a walk-in shower. North-west is a Vastu-preferred spot for toilets.
It now also serves bedroom 2 on this floor. It is ventilated through an obscure-glass window onto the loggia and a high north window.

rooms.name: First-floor hall & landing
notes: You come up the last flight facing the front, and the floor opens to your right: turn right and you are in the hall.
The next flight up starts from this same landing. A 1.2 m slider opens to the loggia, the bathroom is to the left, and ahead the living room, pooja corner and kitchen run in one open space.

rooms.name: Living room
notes: The living room sits in the north of the floor, which Vastu likes for living spaces. The TV is on the north wall between two windows (window, TV, window).
The sofa faces the TV. Behind it a 0.65 m walk runs along the stair screen to the kitchen and bedroom 2, so nobody crosses in front of the TV.
The centre of the plot (Brahmasthan) stays open floor: no walls, columns or plumbing there.

rooms.name: Pooja corner
notes: An open mandir unit stands against the bedroom wall with the idols facing west, so you pray facing east. It sits in the north, with a north window beside it and open floor in front.
No toilet is behind or above it, and the hob is well away.

rooms.name: Kitchen
notes: The kitchen stays in the south-east (Agni corner), the Vastu-preferred spot, with the hob on the east wall so the cook faces east.

The sink is on a slim 1.0 × 0.6 m island parallel to the counter, with a 1.06 m aisle between them. The window over the counter opens for fumes, and the chimney ducts straight out through the east wall.
The fridge and a tall pull-out pantry line the south wall, with overheads and a loft on the east wall.
It is a little smaller than before (about 9.8 m²) because bedroom 2 took the north-east of this floor.

rooms.name: Bedroom 2
notes: Bedroom 2 has moved down to the first floor, at the back in the north-east, so the stair never passes through anyone's room. You reach it past the pooja corner.
A queen bed with its head to the east, a 1.6 m wardrobe with a loft, and windows to the north and east. Vastu suits the north-east for children or study.
It shares the common bathroom at the front of this floor.

rooms.name: Master ensuite
notes: Shower, WC and basin, with a high obscure north window and an exhaust duct. It opens from the bedroom through a pocket slider.
Vastu note: north-centre is a compromise for a toilet (the west and north-west are better, but the front now holds the lounge and stair).

rooms.name: Master suite
notes: The master now takes the whole back half of the floor, about 21 m²: a king bed with its head to the east, an armchair, a writing desk and a 2.6 m wardrobe wall with a dressing table.
Windows face north and east for morning light. You enter from the hall by a pocket slider, and the ensuite is next door.
Vastu note: the south-west, the ideal master corner, holds the stair. The bed faces correctly and the room is in the quieter rear of the house.

rooms.name: Family lounge
notes: A family lounge where everyone can spend time together, right at the top of the stair: turn right off the last step and you are in it.

The second-floor balcony is enclosed: steel-framed glass fills both arches above a 0.45 m sill and opens for breeze. An L-shaped sofa sits under a new north window, with a reading chair and planter by the north arch.
There is no TV. It is a place to talk, read and watch the evening sky. The west glass gets afternoon sun, so use low-e glass and blinds or bamboo chiks inside the arches.

rooms.name: Window-seat bay
notes: A built-in window seat under the south arch, beside the stair landing.

rooms.name: Upper hall & landing
notes: From the landing, the lounge is to your right and a short hall along the stair screen leads to the master suite. The roof flight starts from this same landing.

rooms.name: Stair cabin
notes: The stair arrives inside a small cabin with a west window and a glass skylight over the stairwell. Turn right and step out onto the garden.

rooms.name: Roof garden
notes: Raised planters, a lawn under a timber pergola, a bench and a low table, on the front half of the roof.
The water tank sits on the stair cabin in the south-west, the heavy corner, as Vastu advises. The north-east of the roof is kept light: only solar panels and drying lines.

rooms.name: Drying deck
notes: Drying lines sit in full sun beside raised solar panels.
